To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proto-oncogene Crk is operative downstream of oncogenic KRAS and is activated by PAK1, and that PAK1 is a major effector of oncogenic KRAs in NSCLC.
the KRAS/PAKI/Crk pathway is important in lung cancer progression.

KRAS mutant NSCLC cells express higher levels of p-PAK(Thr423)/p-Crk and lower levels of E-cadherins/p120-catenins compared to KRAS WT cells; and that PAK1 inhibitors and partial inhibitors of other KRAS effecting pathways (i.e., (FTI  +  GGTI)) can dramatically change morphology, proliferation and motility of NSCLC cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of KRAS mutant NSCLC progression.
elucidation of a signaling network downstream of oncogenic KRAS and its implication in lung cancer oncogenesis and metastasis.
the role of proto oncogene c-Crk in the oncogenic signaling of mutant KRAS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PAK1/Crks axis is a key pathway in KRAS mutant lung cancers.
KRAS/PAk1/Crk axis is an important oncogenic pathway that contributes to NSCLC progression and metastasis.
KRAS mutant lung cancers have higher levels of PAK1 phosphorylation and PAK1 phosphorylates Crk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proto-oncogenic c-Crk is an operative downstream effector of KRAS in lung cancers.
PAK1/Crak pathway is a key effector of oncogenic KRAS in NSLC.

KRAS mutant tumors are associated with increased p-PAK/Thr423 and p-Crk/Ser41 and the inhibition of KRAS/ PAK1/CRK axis by PAK1 inhibitors in combination with partial inhibition of other KRAS effecters may provide a novel therapeutic approach for treatment of NSCLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PAK1/Crks axis is an important signaling network in the progression of lung cancer.
targeting the KRAS/PAKA/Crk pathway may have therapeutic potential in the treatment of KRAS mutant NSCLC.
targeting KRAS/PAX1/Crk axis may be a promising approach in the treatment of NSCLC.
